title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): A_0 is an abelian variety over a field k of characteristic p>0. Grothendieck asks when one can attach, functorially in A and compatibly with base change, a k-stratification to H = H^1_dR(A/Λ) for every infinitesimal deformation A/Λ of A_0, with Λ an artinian local k-algebra. A k-stratification is Grothendieck's descent datum along the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal, with no divided powers. Such a structure must be compatible with F: H^(p) → H and V: H → H^(p). He has already argued that this forces A_0 to be ordinary, and that then Im F = Ker V is stable under the stratification.

This page:
(1) Since VF = 0 and, in the ordinary case, Ker V = Im F =: H', the map V vanishes on H'. The image of V is contained in H^{10(p)} = Ker F (the Frobenius twist of the Hodge subspace H^{10} = ω_A). Hence H^{10(p)} is stable under the stratification, because V is horizontal.
(2) Caveat: this does not a priori imply that H^{10} itself is stable. Take Λ complete noetherian local, S = Spf Λ and T = Spf(Λ ⊗̂ Λ) = S × S. Let E_1, E_2 be the two pullbacks of H to T, F_1, F_2 the two pullbacks of H^{10}, and u: E_1 ≅ E_2 the stratification isomorphism.
(3) Stability of the twisted subspace gives u^(p)(F_1^(p)) = F_2^(p), i.e. G^(p) = G'^(p) with G = u(F_1) and G' = F_2. These are T-points of Grass(E) that become equal after pullback along the Frobenius π: T' → T.
(4) In general π is not an epimorphism (T may be non-reduced), so one cannot conclude G = G'. But if S, hence T, is formally smooth over k, Frobenius is faithfully flat, hence an fpqc epimorphism, and G = G'.
(5) Next page: reduce to the case S = M, the formally smooth formal moduli of A_0, and conclude that H^{10} is stable. One gets a functorial, horizontal splitting H = H^{10} ⊕ Im F, i.e. Hodge plus unit-root/conjugate part, which is the ordinary-case splitting. The problem then reduces to stratifying t_A^∨ and t_{A^*}. Grothendieck's closing remark: with plain (non-PD) stratifications, the position of the Hodge filtration relative to the stratification cannot give an infinitesimal classification in characteristic p. This is a no-go which motivates working with divided powers and crystals, i.e. Grothendieck–Messing.

Purpose: this is a test of whether a 'period map' could be built from stratifications (D-module structures with all differential operators) instead of crystals. The answer is essentially negative: the filtration becomes rigid.
errors: The Frobenius-descent step only works when T is formally smooth over k; for artinian Λ, Frobenius on Spf(Λ⊗̂Λ) is not an epimorphism. Grothendieck notices this himself and fixes it on the next page by reducing to the universal formal moduli M, using functoriality and base change.

The claim that an F,V-compatible stratification forces A_0 to be ordinary is stated on the previous page with 'sans doute', i.e. without full proof. The constancy of the geometric type of (H_x, F_x, V_x) along M is the real input, and it is only sketched.
Minor: the transcription reads 'V est une sur H''; the page says 'V est nulle sur H''. This is consistent with VF = 0 and Ker V = Im F.

ideas.what: In the ordinary case Ker V = Im F, and V maps H into H^{10(p)} = Ker F, so a horizontal V forces the Frobenius twist of the Hodge filtration to be horizontal
ideas.modern_name: Transversality of Hodge and conjugate filtrations for ordinary abelian varieties; unit-root splitting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (p-adic properties of modular schemes 1973; Serre–Tate local moduli 1981), Deligne–Illusie, Mazur/Oda for F,V on H^1_dR
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched in Grothendieck's Montreal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74)

ideas.what: Frobenius on a formally smooth k-scheme is faithfully flat, so equality of Frobenius-twisted Grassmannian points implies equality of the points
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius flatness (Kunz) / fpqc descent along Frobenius

ideas.what: No-go remark: with plain stratifications (no divided powers), the position of the Hodge filtration cannot classify infinitesimal deformations in char p
ideas.modern_name: Need for PD-crystals in Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory; F-divided/stratified sheaves are too rigid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1970 ICM / Montreal), Messing 1972; Gieseker 1975 for stratified bundles
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and Montreal lectures; this explicit no-go is unsure

missed.claim: An F,V-compatible functorial stratification forces ordinarity and a horizontal Hodge ⊕ unit-root splitting. In modern terms, only the unit-root part can carry an F-divided (stratified) structure, which matches the later dictionary unit-root F-crystals ↔ étale local systems ↔ F-divided sheaves. Grothendieck reaches this rigidity from the stratification side, as a negative test for a non-PD period map.
missed.quote: Mais si S donc T est formellement lisse sur k, ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: it documents why Grothendieck turned to divided powers and crystals. The mathematics is now standard via Katz and the theory of F-divided sheaves.

deep.surprise_reason: The arguments are correct but routine: horizontality of V, and Frobenius flatness on smooth bases. The conclusion (ordinary splitting; plain stratifications are too rigid) is well known in substance. The page is a nice historical trace of the motivation for PD-crystals, not a lost result.
transcription_corrections: 'rectification' should read 'stratification' throughout ('stable par la stratification envisagée', 'l'iso de stratification').
'V est une sur H'' should read 'V est nulle sur H''.
The interlinear note likely reads '(donc Im F ⊂ Ker V = Im F = H')', not '... = H^1'.
Under T' → T the page reads 'T' = T, puissance p-ième' (T' is T itself via Frobenius); there is no 'T''' on the page.
'on ne peut conclure que G, ...' should be read as 'on ne peut conclure que G = G'' from sections becoming equal after Frobenius base change.
